newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma names candidate for PM.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma names candidate for PM.

text.p: Ukraine's President Leonid Kuchma intends to propose Valery Pustovoitenko, currently minister without portfolio, as the country's next prime minister, a presidential spokesman told independent television on Friday.
Parliament will vote on the nomination next week before going into its summer recess, Roman Bessmertny told Ukrainian television Studio 1+1 after a meeting between Kuchma and parliamentary deputies.
Under Ukraine's constitution 226 deputies in the 450-strong assembly must approve the candidate for prime minister, whose duties are now being carried out by acting premier Vasyl Durdynets.

Pustovoitenko, 50, ran Kuchma's election campaign office in 1994 and the respected Den newspaper said on Friday his appointment could signal the start of Kuchma's next election campaign for October 1999.

The previous prime minister, Pavlo Lazarenko, resigned recently on health grounds, though few believe he was actually ill. Kuchma is keen to speed up economic reforms but faces strong opposition from the more conservative parliament.
